summary: Wrote pnr/floorplan.json (core_utilization_pct=40 with reasons for utilization, pins, power grid, clock/reset) and pnr/pin_order.cfg (West: a, b, op; East: result, flags; North: clk; South: rst_n). No tool was run by me; floorplan, pin placement and PDN checks are pending the runtime.
assumptions: No pin ordering constraint beyond side assignment is required; bit order within a bus is left to OpenLane.
Pin patterns are matched from the start of the pin name (OpenLane uses re.match), so 'a.*' matches only a[0..7] and not flag_* pins.
Power grid uses the PDK default SKY130 PDN as instructed; no strap values are overridden.
Pre-layout ss-corner setup slack of 2.917 ns is enough that a slightly lower utilization (longer wires) does not threaten timing; real STA decides.
Total pins = 33: clk, rst_n, a[7:0], b[7:0], op[2:0], result[7:0], flag_z, flag_c, flag_v, flag_n, as in spec.yaml interfaces.
open_issues: Die is very small (~70 um core); if the default PDN strap pitch does not fit or leaves rows unpowered, the real PDN check will show it and utilization may need lowering within range.
If OpenLane's parser matches patterns unanchored (search instead of match), 'a.*' would also match flag_* pins; the runtime's pin check would report this.

self_assessment.reason: Choices are within the given ranges and follow the arch data flow, but no tool has run yet; pattern matching semantics and small-die PDN fit are confirmed only by the runtime checks.
